item.title: I wish to draw your attention to a silver birch at the top of Wellesley Road near where it joins West drive and adjacent to Dunally School. This has grown very tall and there is a lot of movement even in moderate winds. I refer you to photos I took just the other day. I have been told by Cheltenham Council that you are responsible for trees that are on roadsides. I do not wish to see it cut down as I fully recognise the importance of trees to the urban enviroment, and that the silver birch is a feature of the town, but I believe, and I hope you will agree, that some pruning is urgently necessary, especially as all forcasters have predicted that the storms this winter could be exceptionally severe. I suggest therefore that the top be cut back by at least 10 metres. If it were closer in height to the trees on the corner of Wellesley Road and West Drive it would be less likely to break in high winds. I enclose therefore some photos suggesting the changes which would provide a safer enviroment to both the school and adjacent properties., 3rd September

item.title: Large dip in the road, 3rd September
item.description:
The dip is on the left hand side of the road driving towards Stoke Orchard. A traffic cone was temporarily placed there, but has since disappeared. Now a signpost is there, but obscured by grass and not enough visibility to make a difference. It’s a huge dip, causing many people to swerve and producing a crash hazard. Alternatively causing a car suspension spring to break. It’s been present for many weeks now. It needs levelling out, a sign is unfortunately still a huge hazard and dangerous!
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Main Road, Tewkesbury

item.title: Dangerous gate has been placed across public footpath, leading from Pheasant lane up to the fields at the back of Fiddlers Green Farm., 3rd September
item.description:
Footpath halfway down Pheasant Lane GL51 0XX The owner of Fiddlers Green Farm, who does not own the lane has placed a gate part way across the public footpath and blocking/making access difficult for emergency vechicles and access for other users to their garden and fields. The gate swings in the wind and can easily injure a walker, animal or damage vechicles. the police advised that the wording on the gate is very intimidating, told us to report to yourselves. Please arrange for the gate to be removed before accidents happen. This gate in the wind knocked into my leg causing significant bruising, i felt lucky this time.
